clauses.raw_text: Liquidation Preference: On any liquidation or sale of the Company, the Series A Preferred will first receive 3.0x the Original Purchase Price plus declared but unpaid dividends, and will then participate with the Common Stock pro rata on an as-converted basis, without any cap.
Anti-Dilution: The Series A Preferred will have full-ratchet anti-dilution protection. If the Company later issues shares at a lower price, the conversion price will be reduced to that lower price.
Board of Directors: The Board will consist of five members: three designated by the Series A investors, one designated by the Founders, and one independent director designated by the Board.
Founder Vesting: All Founder shares will be re-vested over 48 months with an 18-month cliff starting at closing. Unvested shares are repurchased at cost on termination for any reason.

Protective Provisions: The consent of a majority of the Series A Preferred is required to sell the Company, create a senior or equal class of stock, or amend the charter in a way that adversely affects the Series A.
Information Rights: Major Investors will receive annual audited and quarterly unaudited financial statements and an annual budget.
No-Shop: For 60 days after signing, the Company will not solicit or negotiate any competing financing or sale of the Company.
Expenses: The Company will pay the reasonable fees and expenses of investor counsel, up to $50,000.

flags.title: Liquidation multiple above 1x
flags.explanation: Investors would take 3.0x their money back before common stockholders (founders) see anything. The market norm is 1x.
flags.market_standard_source: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Liquidation Preference: 1x is the typical multiple

justification.market_norm_cite: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Liquidation Preference: 1x is the typical multiple

flags.title: Uncapped participating preferred
flags.explanation: After taking 3.0x, investors also share in what is left with no cap (double-dipping). Non-participating, or participating with a cap, is the norm.
flags.market_standard_source: NVCA Enhanced Model Term Sheet, Liquidation Preference: participation frequency data

justification.market_norm_cite: NVCA Enhanced Model Term Sheet, Liquidation Preference: participation frequency data

flags.title: Full-ratchet anti-dilution
flags.explanation: In a down round, the investor's conversion price resets to the new lower price regardless of how many shares are sold, which can wipe out founder ownership.
flags.market_standard_source: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Anti-Dilution: broad-based weighted average is the standard

justification.market_norm_cite: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Anti-Dilution: broad-based weighted average is the standard

flags.title: Investors control the board
flags.explanation: Investors hold 3 of 5 seats, and the founders plus the independent director cannot outvote them.
flags.market_standard_source: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Voting Rights / Board of Directors

justification.market_norm_cite: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Voting Rights / Board of Directors

flags.title: Cliff longer than 12 months
flags.explanation: An 18-month cliff means a founder who leaves before month 18 keeps nothing. The norm is a 12-month cliff.
flags.market_standard_source: Market norm: 12-month cliff on a 4-year schedule

justification.market_norm_cite: Market norm: 12-month cliff on a 4-year schedule

flags.title: Founders removable with loss of equity
flags.explanation: Because investors control the board and the founders' shares re-vest, the board could remove a founder and repurchase their unvested shares at cost.
flags.market_standard_source: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Board of Directors and Founder Vesting

justification.market_norm_cite: NVCA Model Term Sheet, Board of Directors and Founder Vesting

flags.title: No-shop longer than 45 days
flags.explanation: A 60-day no-shop stops you talking to other investors for longer than the usual 30 to 45 days, which weakens your negotiating position.

summaries.summary_text: Investors get 3x their investment back first, then also share in the remaining proceeds with no cap.
If you raise money later at a lower price, the investor's shares convert as if they had bought at that lower price.
The board has 5 seats: 3 chosen by investors, 1 by founders and 1 independent.
Founder shares vest over 48 months with an 18-month cliff, and the company can buy back unvested shares at cost if a founder leaves.
Investors must approve a company sale, a new senior or equal share class, or harmful charter changes.
Large investors receive annual audited accounts, quarterly accounts and a yearly budget.
You cannot seek competing offers for 60 days after signing.
The company pays up to $50,000 of the investor's legal costs. (Deliberately marked unverified in the mock data to exercise the warning badge.)
